labeling_rubric.source: attacker-influenced input at a genuine external boundary for pass 3. In this codebase the URL-bearing web boundary is the operator/privilege-gated config API: PUT /api/v1/connection/{key}/secrets (unvalidated_secrets body, scope CONNECTION_CREATE_OR_UPDATE, verify=True triggers the outbound test request immediately), PUT /api/v1/connection/{key}/saas_config, and the messaging config endpoints (scope MESSAGING_CREATE_OR_UPDATE); the persisted values resurface as ConnectionConfig.secrets / get_saas_config() / MessagingConfig.details reads in the service layer. Because these boundaries require an OAuth client scope, source labels carry classification 'candidate' (not tp): untrusted reachability is conditional on holders of those scopes being treated as untrusted. CLI/env/toml configuration (config.cli.server_url, --org-url options) and request headers that never reach an outbound URL are NOT sources.
labeling_rubric.sink: server-side issuance of a network request whose target URL can carry the boundary data above: the URL argument positions of requests/httpx calls, Session/Client.send sites, and the AuthenticatedClient/FidesClient constructor calls that receive the base URI later interpolated into every request URL (field-mediated surrogate sinks). Fetches whose URL is a string literal or derives solely from trusted CLI/env configuration are 'none'. Host-pinned fetches with config-derived path segments remain 'candidate' sinks for recall.
labeling_rubric.sanitizer: proven neutralization for the pass (scheme/host allow-lists, private-IP blocking, redirect control). None were present in the CSVs and none were invented: verified that HttpsSchema.url is a plain str with no URL validation (connections_secrets_https.py:14) and no scheme/host/private-IP checks exist on any outbound path in this tree.
labeling_rubric.summary: internal helper/wrapper flow needed for realistic propagation: the connector_registry_service template-instantiation step that copies ConnectionConfig.secrets into a new SaaSConfig.
labeling_rubric.none: unrelated to CWE-918 in this codebase: trusted operator CLI/env/toml configuration, request headers used for logging/audit/locale/content-type only, credentials placed in headers/bodies/auth tuples rather than URLs, OAuth state/token bookkeeping, URLs built only to be returned to the API client (not fetched server-side), fixed-literal URLs, DB-protocol (mongodb/postgres/...) connection strings, and SDK-internal network I/O fed from operator-side configuration.
labeling_rubric.classification_semantics: tp means the labeled ROLE is genuinely played by the API for pass 3 (a real URL-argument transport call, or a real boundary read feeding a URL position); it does NOT mean a confirmed exploitable vulnerability. fp means the candidate was judged not to play the role. candidate/unknown reserved for plausible-but-conditional roles (privilege-gated config sources, constructor surrogate sinks, host-pinned fetches).
